4.78.m: Pārvatī said:
O Śambhu, which liṅga in the Ānandakānana promotes merit,
merely by the recollection of whose name the great sins are destroyed,
which is always to be served by spiritual practitioners, where supreme delight resides,

4.78.s: yatra dattaṃ hutaṃ japtaṃ dhyātaṃ bhavati cākṣayam .. 2 ..
4.78.d: यत्र दत्तं हुतं जप्तं ध्यातं भवति चाक्षयम् .. 2 ..
4.78.m: and where what is given, offered in fire, muttered, and meditated upon becomes imperishable,
merely by remembering which, by beholding which liṅga,
by bowing before which liṅga, and also by touching it,
and by worshipping it preceded by ceremonial baths with the five nectars and the like,
tell of that liṅga, O Īśāna, so that an unbroken succession of blessings may arise.
Skanda said:
Having heard what was thus spoken by the goddess, O pitcher-born one,
what was declared by the omniscient one, that I shall declare to you; listen!
The God of gods said:
O Umā, that which has been asked by you, which brings release from the bondage of existence—
therefore I shall declare that liṅga; be steady-minded.
And here in the Ānandakānana is my supreme secret;

4.78.s: na mayā kasyacitkhyātaṃ na praṣṭuṃ vetti kaścana ..7..
4.78.d: न मया कस्यचित्ख्यातं न प्रष्टुं वेत्ति कश्चन ..7..
4.78.m: it has not been revealed by me to anyone, nor does anyone know how to ask about it.
There are many liṅgas in my Ānandavana, O beloved;

4.78.s: paraṃ tvayā yathā pṛṣṭaṃ yathāvattadbravīmi te .. 8 ..
4.78.d: परं त्वया यथा पृष्टं यथावत्तद्ब्रवीमि ते .. 8 ..
4.78.m: yet as asked by you, I shall tell you of it as it truly is.

4.78.m: Where you yourself, whose nature is liberation, dwell, O all-pervading one;
where your son also is, [and] the sacred field that destroys obstacles;
by whom also, when I desired victory in the battle with Tripura,
the hope of victory was fulfilled through praise and the offering of many modakas;
where there is a sacred ford that removes sins and increases the pleasure of the ancestors,
from bathing in which the slayer of Vṛtra was freed from the sin of slaying Vṛtra;
where even the King of Dharma attained the office of dispenser of justice,
having performed difficult austerity with supreme absorption—
Where even birds attained knowledge that releases from the cycle of rebirth,
where the delightful banyan tree became golden. // 13
Simply by the darśana of which liṅga, a king named Durdama,
though an oppressor of the worlds, instantly became of virtuous mind. // 14
Listen, O beautiful lady, I shall describe the māhātmya
and the manifestation of that liṅga, which destroys great sins. // 15
Here in my Ānandavana, that seat is designated as the seat of Dharma;
merely by the darśana of that seat, a man is freed from sins. // 16
Long ago, Yama, the son of Vivasvat, of supreme self-control,
performed extensive tapas before you, O large-eyed lady. // 17
Standing in the midst of water in the cold season, exposed to the open sky in the rains,
and standing amid five fires in the hot season, he thus performed tapas at times. // 18
Touching the ground only with the big toe of his foot, he stood for a long time;
standing on one foot, he too [remained] for a long time at times. // 19
He subsisted on air, [and thus] endured many allotted times;
when thirsty, he drank only drops of water from the tips of kuśa grass. // 20
Thus performing tapas, he spent a celestial period of four yugas,
fourfold, desirous of seeing me through supreme concentration. // 21
Then, pleased with the tapas of that steady-minded one,
I went to grant boons to that noble-minded Śamana. // 22
There was a banyan named Kāñcanaśākha, which dispelled the heat of the sun
with its pleasant shade, and was a shelter to many birds. // 23
With its sprout-like leaves swaying in the gentle, gentle breeze like slender hands,
dispelling exhaustion, it seemed to invite travelers scorched by the road. // 24
With its own ripe, fragrant, and sweet fruits, red by nature,
it would abundantly gratify the company of seekers. // 25
Seeing beneath it that supreme son of the sun,
his body motionless as a post, his eyes fixed on the tip of his nose, // 26
surrounded on all sides by the rising splendor of his tapas,
like the sun in the deep blue sky by its own radiance, // 27
having installed with great devotion a great liṅga marked with his own name,
as if worshipped with masses of light made of clear sunstones, // 28
and performing great tapas as though taking that liṅga as a witness,
I spoke to Dharmarāja, saying, “O son of the sun, choose a boon! // 29
Enough of your tapas, O fortunate one! I am pleased, O you of noble vows!”

4.78.m: the shore of the shoreless, the grantor of the farther shore of the supreme ocean, to you who bear the moon on your crest, homage! // 33

4.78.s: kālātparastvaṃ prakṛteḥ parastvaṃ kālāya kālātprakṛte namaste ..34 ..
4.78.d: कालात्परस्त्वं प्रकृतेः परस्त्वं कालाय कालात्प्रकृते नमस्ते ..34 ..
4.78.m: you are beyond time, you are beyond nature. Homage to you who are Time, beyond time and beyond nature! // 34

Your form is the self; your form is the supreme Self; you are the inner Self of all moving and unmoving beings. // 35
From you is the world; you are the world manifest; the world is yours, O sole friend of the world!

4.78.s: hartāvitā tvaṃ prathamo vidhātā vidhātṛviṣṇvīśa namo namaste .. 36 ..
4.78.d: हर्ताविता त्वं प्रथमो विधाता विधातृविष्ण्वीश नमो नमस्ते .. 36 ..
4.78.m: You are the destroyer, the protector, and the first creator. O Creator, Viṣṇu, and Lord, homage, homage to you! // 36
You alone are Mṛḍa to those who walk the Vedic path; you alone are Bhīma to those who walk outside the Vedic path.
You are Śaṃkara to those possessing good devotion to Soma; you are fierce Rudra to those lacking devotion. // 37

4.78.m: Homage to you, O Śaṃkara, tranquil Śambhu! Homage to you adorned with the crescent moon!

4.78.s: sa eva dhanyastava bhaktibhāgyastavārcako yaḥ sukṛtī sa eva ..

4.78.m: he who always praises you is praised by the gods led by Duścyavana. // 40
Who here is able to praise you, O infinite power—one like me of slight intellectual power?

4.78.d: प्राचां न वाचामिहगोचरो यः स्तुतिस्त्वयीयं नतिरेव यावत् .. 41 ..

Skanda said:

4.78.m: Having uttered [this], the son of the Sun, with supreme devotion, repeatedly chanting, “Homage to Śiva,”
his head touching the earth, exceedingly delighted, bowed down a thousand times to Śambhu.

4.78.m: Then Śiva, the Lord, restrained him, who was utterly exhausted by austerity, from those prostrations,

4.78.m: and granted boons to the son of the Seven-Horsed [Sun]: “Become Dharmarāja even by name.
You alone shall hold authority over righteousness for all embodied beings, both stationary and moving.

4.78.s: mayā niyuktodya dinādikṛtyaḥ praśādhi sarvānmama śāsanena ..44..
4.78.d: मया नियुक्तोद्य दिनादिकृत्यः प्रशाधि सर्वान्मम शासनेन ..44..
4.78.m: Appointed by me today to administer duties beginning with the day, govern all according to my command.

4.78.s: tvaṃ dakṣiṇāyāśca diśodhināthastvaṃ karmasākṣī bhava sarvajaṃtoḥ ..

4.78.m: Be the presiding lord of the southern direction; be the witness to the deeds of every living creature.
Shown the path by you, let the highest and the lowest go from here to the destination suited to their own deeds.
Because this liṅga was thoroughly worshipped here by you, who are devoted to me, O Dharma,

The mortal with pure intellect who beholds Dharmeśvara even once,

4.78.m: And the men who recite this hymn uttered by you anywhere before you,

4.79.m: Skanda said:
Beholding him with throat choked by tears of bliss,

4.79.s: mṛḍaḥ pasparśa pāṇibhyāṃ saudhābhyāṃ tu sudhāṃbudhiḥ .. 1 ..
4.79.d: मृडः पस्पर्श पाणिभ्यां सौधाभ्यां तु सुधांबुधिः .. 1 ..
4.79.m: Mṛḍa, an ocean of nectar, touched him with both nectar-like hands.
Then, through the delight of that touch, Dharmarāja, of great austerity,
made his body, burnt by the fire of austerity, sprout once again.
Then that son of the Sun spoke to the god of gods, the lord of Umā,
who had a gracious countenance, was serene, and was surrounded by serene attendants:
“If you are pleased, O Īśāna, omniscient one, treasure of compassion,
what need is there for another boon here, since you have been made visible to me?

4.79.s: yaṃ na vedā viduḥ samyaṅna ca tau vedapūruṣau ..
4.79.d: यं न वेदा विदुः सम्यङ्न च तौ वेदपूरुषौ ..
4.79.m: Whom the Vedas do not truly know, nor do those two beings of the Veda—
yet if I am worthy of a boon from you, then, O Lord, I pray:
O Śrīkaṇṭha, be the granter of a boon to these fledglings of an egg-born bird, sweet of voice,
who were long witnesses to my austerity, who took birth before me,
bereft of both parents, knowers of history and traditional lore,
parrots that have renounced food and roaming.
At the time of giving birth to these, afflicted by disease,
the female parrot met her death, and the male parrot was eaten by a hawk.
Protect these orphans who always look upon my face,
O lord of orphans, by you who are the very embodiment of remaining life!”
Having heard these words of Dharma, spotless with benevolence for others,
and having summoned them, O sage, whose faces were bowed down with modesty,

4.81.m:
Agastya said:
What is the māhātmya of Dharmatīrtha as related by the god Śambhu
to the Goddess, O Skanda? Tell that; show grace! // 1
Skanda said:
O crusher of the Vindhya's height, I shall relate the origin of Dharmatīrtha.
Listen, O wise one, as spoken by the god. // 2
Having slain Vṛtra, the enemy of Vṛtra incurred [the sin of] murdering a brahmin.
Repentant, he then questioned his family priest regarding expiation. // 3
Bṛhaspati said:
If you, O king of the gods, wish to dispel this brahmin-murder
so difficult to abandon, then go to Kāśī, protected by the Lord of the Universe. // 4
Nothing else is anywhere seen as a sovereign medicine for brahmin-murder
apart from the supreme capital of the Lord of the Universe, O Śakra. // 5
Where the head of Brahmā fell from the tip of Bhairava's hand—
go quickly to that Ānandavana, O enemy of Vṛtra! // 6
Upon merely reaching the border of Ānandavana, O Śakra,
the murder of a brahmin flees, trembling and destitute of refuge. // 7
Of other sins too, even of those committed by great sinners,
supreme Kāśī, presided over by the Lord of the Universe, is the destroyer. // 8
Liberation from heinous sin occurs in Kāśī alone, O Śatakratu;
liberation from the great round of rebirth occurs in Kāśī alone and nowhere else. // 9
Kāśī is the city of nirvāṇa; Kāśī destroys the multitude of all sins;
Kāśī is dear to the Lord of the Universe; heaven is not the equal of Kāśī. // 10
He who fears brahmin-murder, he who fears the cycle of existence,
should never abandon Kāśī, which reveals liberation. // 11
Where, upon the abandoning of the body, the seeds of karma of living beings,
scorched by the glance of Hara, never sprout again. // 12
Having reached that Kāśī, O enemy of Vṛtra, to dispel the killing of Vṛtra,
worship the Lord of the Universe, who bestows liberation to the universe. // 13
Having heard this speech of Bṛhaspati, the thousand-eyed [Indra]
went swiftly to Kāśī, the destroyer of heinous sins. // 14
Having bathed in the northward-flowing [Gaṅgā] and staying near Dharmeśa,
he worshipped Mahādeva to dispel the murder of the brahmin. // 15
Intent on the chanting of the Mahārudra, Sutrāman then beheld the three-eyed Lord
situated within the liṅga, illuminating the sky with his own luster. // 16
Again he praised him in manifold ways with Rudrasūktas taught in the Veda.
Then, having issued forth and appeared from the liṅga, Bhava said: // 17
"O consort of Śacī, I am pleased; choose a boon, O one of noble vows!
What should be given? Speak quickly, O you who have taken your seat at the seat of Dharma!" // 18
Having heard these loving words of the God of gods, Hari,
the slayer of Vṛtra, spoke to him: "O omniscient one, what is unknown to you?" // 19
Then, moved by his grace, through the resort to the seat of Dharma,
the Lord created a sacred ford there and said: "Bathe here, O Indra!" // 20
There, merely by Indra's bathing, he instantly became fragranced with divine perfume,
and he regained his previous handsome splendor derived from a hundred sacrifices. // 21
Seeing that wonder, the sages, Nārada and others,
bathed joyfully in the Dharmatīrtha, which removes sin. // 22
They satiated the divine ancestors and performed ancestral rites with faith;
they bathed Dharmeśa with pots filled with water from that sacred ford. // 23
From then on, that sacred ford has been renowned as Dharmāndhu,
the supreme, effortless cleanser of sins such as the murder of a brahmin. // 24
Whatever fruit is proclaimed from bathing in the king of sacred fords [Prayāga],
that becomes a thousandfold merely by bathing in Dharmāndhu. // 25
Whatever fruit a mortal attains at Gaṅgādvāra, at Kurukṣetra, or at the confluence of the Gaṅgā and the ocean,
he would attain that at Dharmatīrtha. // 26
Whatever fruit would be attained by bathing in the Narmadā, the Sarasvatī, or the Gautamī when Jupiter is in Leo,
he would attain that at the well of Dharma. // 27
Whatever fruit there would be from bathing in the sacred ford at Mānasa, Puṣkara, Dvārikā, and the ocean,
that would be at the reservoir of Dharma. // 28
Whatever fruit is obtained at Sūkarakṣetra on the full-moon day of Kārttika, at the great pool of Gaurī in Caitra,
or on the day of Hari at Śaṅkhoddhāra, that fruit is attained here. // 29
The ancestors wait for men who desire to bathe at two sacred fords—
at the Gaṅgā and at the well of Dharma—with the hope of receiving the offering of rice-balls. // 30
Either near Pitāmaha or in front of Dharmeśa,
at the Phalgu and at the well of Dharma, the great-grandfathers rejoice. // 31
Having bathed in the well of Dharma and fully satiated the grandfathers,
what more could a man accomplish by going to Gayā to bring joy to the ancestors? // 32
Just as grandfathers would be satisfied at Gayā through the offering of rice-balls,
so indeed would they be at Dharmatīrtha—neither less nor more. // 33

As if another comet had arisen among his own subjects,
king Durdama existed merely for untimely destruction.
Once, afflicted by the vice of hunting game,
accompanied by hunters, riding a horse, pursuing behind a young cow, he entered the forests.
Alone by the turn of fate, that king Durdama, / armed with a bow and mounted on his steed, entered Ānandakānana.
Then, seeing everywhere trees with fresh foliage,
affording pleasant shade and of vast expanse, he became as if free of fatigue.
With fragrant, pleasantly cool, deeply exhilarating, and gentle wind,
the king was fanned for a moment by the trees using sprout-fans.
Not only did his fatigue born of hunting depart,
but the weariness born from his very birth vanished upon beholding that forest.
In the midst of the forest he saw a temple that kissed the sky,

Then, dismounting from his horse, that king, exceedingly astonished,
reached the pavilion of Dharmeśa and praised himself:
“Blessed am I! Joyful am I! Blessed are my eyes today!
Blessed is this day of mine, since I have seen this ground!
Then again he reproached himself by the power of the seat of dharma:
“Fie on me, in company with wicked people, having abandoned the association of the virtuous!
Causing distress to living beings, foolish, skilled in oppressing my subjects,
finding pleasure by stealing the wives and wealth of others!
Until today my life has gone in vain, small-minded that I am,
since nowhere had such abodes of dharma been seen by me!”
Having thus reproached himself greatly, and having bowed to the all-pervading Dharmeśvara,
king Durdama mounted his horse and went to his own realm.

4.83.m: The queen said: / “Pay attention, O lord of the earth; I shall narrate in accordance with truth / the procedure of this observance, its fruit, and its presiding deity. / Formerly, before the wife of the bestower of wealth [Kubera], chief among fortunate women, by Brahmā’s son, / Nārada, this observance was proclaimed for one desiring a son. / And it was performed by that goddess, and Nalakūbara became her son; / by many other women as well, sons have been obtained through this observance and others. / Here Gaurī, knowing every ritual procedure, should be worshipped according to the rite, / accompanied by an infant nursing at her upturned breast. / On the third day of the bright fortnight of the month of Mārgaśīrṣa, upon a water-pot / having placed a copper vessel filled completely with grains of rice, / and placing over the vessel an unbroken, new garment, dyed with turmeric, / exceedingly fine, surpassing all others in fineness; / upon that, a handsome lotus opened by the rays of the sun; / upon the pericarp of that, fashioned of four gold pieces, / one should worship the image with devotion, with jewels, silken garments, and the like, / with delightful flowers of various kinds, with fruits, prominent among which are oranges, / with fragrant scents such as sandalwood and the like, camphor, and musk, / with food offerings such as sweet rice, and cooked foods of many varieties, / and with incense, prominent among which is agarwood, in a charming bower of flowers. / At night, a vigil should be kept, remaining awake amidst supreme celebrations. / In an altar fire-pit measuring one cubit, with the verse beginning with ‘Jātavedas’, / bathing [offerings] in clarified butter and honey, the twice-born priest knowing the mantras should make offerings, / using a thousand blossoming lotus flowers himself. / A brown cow that has newly calved, gentle-natured, and yielding abundant milk, / adorned with ornaments and possessing auspicious marks, he should give to the preeminent teacher. / The husband and wife, having fasted with devotion, adorned in new garments, / having bathed in the morning on the fourth day, honoring the teacher with reverence, / full of joy, with garments, ornaments, garlands, and priestly fees, / should offer that idol together with all ritual accessories to the teacher.”

4.83.m: Having obtained a supreme kingdom difficult for all kings to attain, / and having enjoyed vast pleasures, in the end you will attain perfection. / The charming city of Vārāṇasī is [famed] throughout the entire earth. / Even there, the confluence of the rivers [Asi and Gaṅgā] on the chest of Gaṅgā is meritorious. / Even beyond that, the sacred ford Hayagrīva is exceedingly merit-bestowing, / where Viṣṇu Hayagrīva grants whatever the devotee contemplates. / Far superior even to the Hayagrīva sacred ford is Gajatīrtha, / where by mere ablution one obtains the fruit of donating an elephant. / And more merit-bestowing than Gajatīrtha is Kokāvarāhatīrtha; / having worshipped Kokāvarāha there, a person incurs no rebirth. / Even beyond Kokāvarāha, near Dilīpeśvara, / is the most excellent Dilīpatīrtha, supreme and immediately removing sins. / Beyond that is Sagaratīrtha, near Sagareśa, / bathing where a person will not sink again into the ocean of sorrow. / And better than Sagaratīrtha is Saptasāgaratīrtha, / bathing where a person attains the merit arising from ablutions in the seven oceans. / Renowned beyond Saptābdhitīrtha is the sacred ford called Mahodadhi, / immersed in which once, a wise man burns up the great ocean of sins. / Beyond that is the meritorious Cauratīrtha, near Kapileśvara, / bathing where the sin of stealing gold and the like goes to destruction. / Beyond that, near Kedāreśvara, is the praiseworthy Haṃsatīrtha, / where, taking the form of a swan, I lead embodied souls to Brahmā. / Beyond that is the exceedingly merit-bestowing sacred ford of Keśava named Tribhuvana, / immersed in which mortals do not enter the mortal realm [again]. / And even greater than that is the Govyāghreśvara sacred ford, / where both attained perfection, abandoning their natural enmity. / Even better than that, O hero, is the sacred ford named Māndhātṛ, / where that king obtained the rank of universal emperor.

4.83.m: Even beyond that is the sacred ford named Mucukunda, exceedingly merit-bestowing, / bathing where a man is never overcome by enemies. / Beyond that, towering higher, is Pṛthutīrtha, the supreme means for attaining blessings, / where seeing Pṛthvīśvara, a man becomes a lord of the earth. / Beyond that is the sacred ford of Paraśurāma, bestowing great success, / where the son of Jamadagni was freed from the sin of slaying the kṣatriyas.
